result.title: Geo-SMILE: Statistical Model-Agnostic Interpretability with Local Explanations for Geospatial Machine Learning
result.comment: This manuscript is derived from MSc by Research thesis work in Computer Science at the University of Hull, United Kingdom. Source code is publicly available
result.summary: Conventional post-hoc explanation methods were developed largely for non-spatial inputs and often provide limited explicit treatment of geographic context. We introduce Geo-SMILE, a model-agnostic framework that distinguishes substantive Feature explanation from geographic-position response through complementary perturbation branches. The Feature branch masks substantive predictors while retaining observed coordinates; the Geo branch relocates geographic units while holding substantive predictors fixed. Following the statistical-distance-weighted surrogate principle of SMILE, input-distribution Wasserstein distances determine coalition locality weights and weighted Ridge surrogates approximate expected black-box predictions. GeoSensitivity, signed in the keep orientation, quantifies fitted-model responses to geographic-player relocation under the specified design. Across crime prediction in Hull, housing-price prediction in Seattle and ride-hailing demand in Chicago, held-out weighted surrogate fidelity ranges from $R_w^2=0.910$ to $0.989$ in the Feature branch and from $0.842$ to $0.906$ in the Geo branch. The framework makes geographic position an explicit object of post-hoc explanation while requiring separate assessment of interpretation, stability and reference dependence.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Geo-SMILE，一个模型无关的事后解释框架，用「实质性特征扰动」与「地理位置迁移」两条互补分支，结合 Wasserstein 距离加权的 Ridge 代理模型，将地理坐标响应从特征贡献中分离出来，并在犯罪、房价与网约车需求数据上评估代理保真度。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按扰动来源分设分支并对预测贡献做加性归因的思路，可能可供核查用于区分 LVR 中内容证据与位置／坐标因素的贡献分配，但该工作面向表格型地理数据、与 VLM 内部状态无直接关联，迁移可行性需较多核查。
